purpose: Purchasable Beelink system variant built around the already-tracked AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S platform. This record focuses on system-level networking, storage, thermals, pricing, and vendor LLM evidence rather than treating Strix Halo as a new architecture.

hardware.product: GTR9 Pro AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395
hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 16C/32T Zen 5, up to 5.1GHz
hardware.storage: 2TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe included; 2x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 slots; vendor states up to 8TB per slot / 16TB total

physical.cooling: dual-fan MSC2.0 system with full-surface vapor chamber and 137mm heat fins

processor_power_w.evidence: AMD platform specification plus Beelink vendor system setting; neither value is whole-system wall power

quantization_compatibility.gguf: practical through CPU/Vulkan/ROCm-capable llama.cpp-family paths; exact GPU acceleration depends on OS, driver, runtime, and UMA allocation
quantization_compatibility.low_bit: 4-bit and 5-bit quantized LLMs are especially relevant for 70B-class models; Q8 workloads are practical for smaller models such as the vendor-published Qwen 32B example
quantization_compatibility.evidence: platform/runtime guidance plus Beelink vendor benchmark

model_size_practicality.assessment: vendor demonstrates Qwen 32B Q8 in LM Studio at 6.23 tok/s
model_size_practicality.caveat: Beelink does not publish enough prompt/context/prefill/decode metadata on the product page for normalized cross-platform benchmarking.

model_size_practicality.assessment: strong capacity fit in 128GB unified memory; Beelink explicitly markets local 70B deployment
model_size_practicality.caveat: Actual speed depends on quantization, context/KV cache, backend, UMA allocation, and sustained memory bandwidth.

model_size_practicality.assessment: capacity can support selected aggressively quantized or sparse/MoE workloads, but fit does not imply interactive decode speed

efficiency.note: These ratios use the processor TDP, not whole-system wall power. The integrated 230W AC PSU makes the system less DC-native than embedded platforms. A manufacturer-hosted customer review reports about 15W idle and up to about 180W during an AI workload on Ubuntu, but this is anecdotal and is not stored as verified system power.

clusterability.note: Dual 10GbE is a meaningful differentiator versus many Strix Halo mini PCs for distributed inference, network-attached model storage, and multi-client serving.

pricing.note: Official page displayed US$4,349 sale price versus US$4,699 reference price and stated pre-sale orders ship within 35 days. Beelink pricing varies by storefront/region and has changed materially over time.

cost_efficiency.note: Capacity-only acquisition metric; excludes SSD, dual-10GbE value, taxes, shipping, and runtime performance.

hardware.notes: Shared Strix Halo silicon. Compare GTR9 Pro against BOSGAME M5, Framework Desktop, GMKtec EVO-X2/X3, Minisforum MS-S1 MAX, GEEKOM A9 Mega, and other Ryzen AI Max+ 395 systems primarily on delivered price, 10GbE networking, cooling, storage, warranty, and measured wall power.
